native_boundary: Existing NSMenu autoenable and performKeyEquivalent, NSApplication targetForAction/sendAction, and native field command delegation.
application_boundary: Actual HTMLInputElement::GetControllers at 0x589119c; GetControllerForCommand and IsCommandEnabled use the actual collection/controller vtables (+24), with Release at +16. Command execution reuses the existing TextControlState DoCommandCallback.
compiled_guards: GetControllers first 20 bytes added to the exact-build command guard. Existing build ID, command callback, command-name and modifier guards remain.
findings: Native Paste validation consults its own pasteboard. A browser's valid clipboard can coexist with empty unfocused helper storage, so post-action selector reporting alone cannot enable Paste.

The generic application callback supplies validation and execution at the existing native target/responder boundary. The native menu owns key matching, validation dispatch and action dispatch; the host does not add menu items, shortcut bindings or clipboard data.
Unclaimed commands return -1 and retain their original native target and validator. Claimed commands execute once in the application; native mutation/copy is suppressed.

The optional C API appends one function pointer, keeping ABI 1 and earlier input/pointer/text capability values. The transport advertises command support independently and reuses the registered owner callback channel.

The actual native text-view default menu contains Cut, Copy and Paste but no Undo item. A retained Alt+Z probe inserted z. Native application Edit-menu binding remains required; this change does not add a replacement shortcut table.

Command and edit callbacks share one channel. Validate each reply by its own magic/result contract, drain valid older serials, and require the expected magic for the current serial. An isolated helper retaining the earlier strict-magic-first reader loses the following edit in the mixed-reply probe.

A test waiting only for unchanged expected clipboard text did not prove that native TextEdit had processed its new Copy. The fixture now observes a new native pasteboard change count as well as the expected text before returning focus, and retains native Wayland publication logs. Rapid focus/clipboard-owner transitions remain a separate lifecycle requirement.
